The lights stay on and the water stays hot

Kariba’s power and water can fluctuate. Here is how the lodge copes, so nothing surprises you.

Standby power

A 6.5 kVA generator backs up the municipal grid.

Hot water

Solar geysers with an electric backup for cloudy days.

Drinking water

Tap water is municipal and not for drinking. Bottled or purified water is provided.

Your own chef

Main Lodge guests can choose full catering from an à la carte menu, or self-cater and still use the chef at no extra charge.

Pool, bar and verandah

A central pool with a lapa, bar and braai area, shared across the estate.

Safe and looked after

A fully walled estate with daily housekeeping in every home.

Around the estate

A walled hilltop with a pool, gardens and a view across the water.

Kariba is why you came

Tigerfish charters

Fresh-water sport fishing for tigerfish, tilapia bream and vundu, arranged through the lodge.

Sunset on the verandah

The hilltop faces west across the lake, so dinner comes with the best seat in town.

Catch of the day

Land bream on a charter and the chef will cook it for dinner.

Game drives

Local drives and land-based safari links, organised by management.

Boat hire and a booze cruise are also on offer, and we arrange airport transfers. The lodge supports The Tashinga Initiative, the Zambezi Elephant Fund, Wild Zambezi and the Kariba Animal Welfare Fund Trust.

What guests keep mentioning

Themes from guest reviews on Airbnb, where the lodge averages 4.29 out of 5.

The view

Guests love the height over the lake and the sunsets from Mica Point.

Happy and the chef

Manager Happy Rukumbo gets praise for attentive service, and the chef’s cooking for the food.

Close to the shops

Grocery stores are within two kilometres, which suits self-catering stays.

Find us on Mica Point

810 Mica Drive, Mica Point, Kariba, Zimbabwe. The lodge sits on the hilltop beside the Kariba Dam Wall.

Check-in from 14:00, check-out by 10:00. Other times can be arranged with management.
